pm_structure.summary: General account is managed in-house by Lifeco's Global Investments function under the EVP & Global CIO (John Melvin, Lifeco/Canada Life), through regional insurer-owned investment teams in Canada, the U.S. (Empower) and Europe (Canada Life Asset Management UK, Irish Life Investment Managers, Setanta), plus GWL Realty Advisors for real estate. Retail asset management is separate: Canada Life Investment Management Ltd. (CLIML, est. 2021) runs Canada Life Mutual Funds largely via sub-advisors, with Power Corp sister Mackenzie (IGM) a core sub-advisor. Private-markets access runs through Power-group affiliates (Northleaf stake with Mackenzie; Sagard) and a strategic partnership with Franklin Templeton created by the 2024 Putnam sale (initial US$25bn GA allocation).

rotation_commentary.text: CIO Melvin (Q2 call): 'conservative, well diversified portfolio... not aggressively chasing' spreads near historic tights; keep risk-taking steady, build portfolio yield via capital-efficient ALM redeployment across segments.

Real estate: ~20% value decline over two years; no active additions to non-par real estate for two years and none intended; a further C$200mm of real estate redeployed into other asset classes after Q2 2026.
CEO Harney: earnings becoming less dependent on trading gains; strategy of 'repositioning the portfolio toward higher-growth, capital-efficient businesses' (Retirement, Wealth, Capital Solutions).
Invested assets C$257.8bn: bonds 70% (98% IG, 70% A or better), private bonds 14%, mortgages 14%; 94% of non-par invested assets in fixed income.
Empower adds private equity, private credit and private real estate to advised DC plans via CITs with Apollo, Franklin Templeton, Goldman, Neuberger, PIMCO, Partners Group, Sagard.
Macro equity tail hedge is contingent only: 'no macro hedge transactions executed and there are currently no assets supporting the macro hedge program'.
Putnam sale to Franklin Templeton completed; Lifeco redirects an initial US$25bn of GA/AUM to Franklin specialist managers, retains PanAgora and ~4.9% FT stake.

governance: Three lines of defence (business/Investment Management = 1st; actuarial, finance, risk, compliance = 2nd; internal audit = 3rd), overseen by the Board

Executive Risk Management Committee chaired by CRO, advised by Market & Credit Risk, Insurance Risk and Operational Risk committees; CRO reports to CEO and Board Risk Committee
